title: The Serpent
html:
• Sutta Nipāta 1.1 Anthology of Discourses 1.1 Sutta Nipāta

Uragasutta The Serpent The Snake

Yo uppatitaṁ vineti kodhaṁ, When anger surges, they drive it out, A monk who removes anger when it appears, Visaṭaṁ sappavisaṁva osadhehi; as with medicine a cobra’s spreading venom. as one removes a serpent’s venom using medicines, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yo rāgamudacchidā asesaṁ, They’ve cut off greed entirely, A monk who completely cuts off passion, Bhisapupphaṁva saroruhaṁ vigayha; like a lotus plucked flower and stalk. like a lotus plant dropping its flowers, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yo taṇhamudacchidā asesaṁ, They’ve cut off craving entirely, A monk who has completely severed craving, Saritaṁ sīghasaraṁ visosayitvā; drying up that swift-flowing stream. who has dried up the swiftly flowing river, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yo mānamudabbadhī asesaṁ, They’ve swept away conceit entirely, A monk who completely destroys conceit, Naḷasetuṁva sudubbalaṁ mahogho; as a fragile bridge of reeds by a great flood. like a flood destroys a fragile bamboo bridge, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yo nājjhagamā bhavesu sāraṁ, In future lives they find no worth, A monk who sees no value in states of being, Vicinaṁ pupphamivā udumbaresu; as an inspector of fig trees finds no flower. as one does not find flowers on fig trees, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yassantarato na santi kopā, They hide no anger within, A monk in whom there is no anger, Itibhavābhavatañca vītivatto; passed beyond any kind of existence. who has completely gone beyond both being and non-being, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yassa vitakkā vidhūpitā, Their mental vibrations are cleared away, A monk who has completely blown away their thoughts, Ajjhattaṁ suvikappitā asesā; internally clipped off entirely. whose mind is internally well-ordered, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yo nāccasārī na paccasārī, They have not run too far nor run back, A monk who neither goes too far nor goes back, Sabbaṁ accagamā imaṁ papañcaṁ; but have gone beyond all this proliferation. who transcends all this complication, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yo nāccasārī na paccasārī, They have not run too far nor run back, A monk who neither goes too far nor goes back, Sabbaṁ vitathamidanti ñatva loke; for they know that nothing in the world is what it seems. who knows that the world is completely false, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yo nāccasārī na paccasārī, They have not run too far nor run back, A monk who neither goes too far nor goes back, Sabbaṁ vitathamidanti vītalobho; knowing nothing is what it seems, free of greed. who is free of greed, knowing it to be completely false, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yo nāccasārī na paccasārī, They have not run too far nor run back, A monk who neither goes too far nor goes back, Sabbaṁ vitathamidanti vītarāgo; knowing nothing is what it seems, free of lust. who is free of passion, knowing it to be completely false, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yo nāccasārī na paccasārī, They have not run too far nor run back, A monk who neither goes too far nor goes back, Sabbaṁ vitathamidanti vītadoso; knowing nothing is what it seems, free of hate. who is free of hatred, knowing it to be completely false, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yo nāccasārī na paccasārī, They have not run too far nor run back, A monk who neither goes too far nor goes back, Sabbaṁ vitathamidanti vītamoho; knowing nothing is what it seems, free of delusion. who is free of delusion, knowing it to be completely false, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yassānusayā na santi keci, They have no underlying tendencies at all, A monk who has no subconscious tendencies, Mūlā ca akusalā samūhatāse; and are rid of unskillful roots, who has eliminated the unwholesome roots, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yassa darathajā na santi keci, They have nothing born of distress at all A monk who has no anxiety whatsoever Oraṁ āgamanāya paccayāse; to make them to return to the near shore. about this life or the next, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yassa vanathajā na santi keci, No snarl grows in them at all, A monk who has no desire whatsoever Vinibandhāya bhavāya hetukappā; that would shackle them to a new life. based on which one might be bound to existence, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇaṁ. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Yo nīvaraṇe pahāya pañca, They’ve given up the five hindrances, A monk who has discarded the five hindrances, Anigho tiṇṇakathaṅkatho visallo; untroubled, rid of indecision, free of thorns. who is untroubled, free of doubt, unafflicted, So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṁ, Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far, relinquishes both the here and the beyond Urago jiṇṇamivattacaṁ purāṇanti. as a serpent its old worn-out skin. like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

Uragasuttaṁ paṭhamaṁ.
